Article Title: Google ex-CEO Eric Schmidt blames technology companies for AI fears in America; says: Millions have experienced Google Gemini firsthand for good, but our industry does a bad job
Article Text:
“Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits,”

“We talk about all the negatives without talking the positives, and people are much more likely to index their minds on the negatives.”

Eric Schmidt wants large data centers away from population centers

“Let me state categorically that large data centers should not be near population centers,”

“Why would this be controversial? And they should have their own power systems. One of the great things about America is we have an awful lot of empty spaces. Put them there.”

Eric Schmidt sees a role for AI in scientific research

Eric Schmidt believes AI companies are underselling the technology’s benefits. After the November US midterms, the former Google CEO told Axios that the industry’s own messaging helps explain why Americans focus on the risks of artificial intelligence (AI). The interview came as proposed data centers, which house the computers that run AI services, faced opposition from communities concerned about electricity costs and environmental effects. Millions of people already use AI tools firsthand. Google’s parent company, Alphabet, reported 950 million monthly active users for its Gemini app in July, which shows how widely the app is being used. A user can find Gemini helpful for a task and still question how a proposed data center could affect their electricity bill.Schmidt said.Schmidt proposed building large data centers in sparsely populated areas and giving them their own power systems.Schmidt said.Concern about those facilities was already growing before the midterms. In September, Pew Research Center reported that more Americans saw data centers as having negative effects on home energy costs and the environment than earlier in the year. A separate June survey found that 71% of US adults expected AI to lead to fewer jobs in the country over the next 20 years, up from 64% in 2024. Pew data center survey,Schmidt pointed to scientific research as an area where AI could help. He said he expects professors, graduate students and postdoctoral researchers to work alongside AI agents, software that can carry out assigned tasks. He cited recent progress in mathematics and highlighted the role of human supervision in AI-assisted problem solving.
Article Summary: Eric Schmidt believes AI companies are underselling the technology’s benefits. The former Google CEO wants large data centers away from population centers. “Our industry does a terrible job of marketing our benefits,” Schmidt said. Schmidt pointed to scientific research as an area where AI could help.

Article Title: Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos says that thousands of layoffs has made the company healthier for the future; adds: But yes 'my heart ...'
Article Text:
Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos

Ted Sarandos balances empathy with business strategy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Netflix layoffs : What co-CEOs said after 1000 job cuts

Netflix Co-CEO Ted Sarandos has opened up about the streaming giant’s decision to cut thousands of jobs, calling the move a difficult but necessary step that leaves the business stronger going forward. Speaking in his first interview since the layoffs took place, Sarandos explained that the reductions followed years of continuous expansion across the company’s large workforce. While routine staffing adjustments are common in the corporate world, he noted that Netflix had not carried out a restructuring of this scale in roughly five years.“We have a very large employee base, and we've been growing and growing and growing, and many companies routinely will go through and do these kinds of things, these kinds of adjustments. We haven't done something like this in about five years, so it was a readjustment of a lot of groups within Netflix, who do what we do every day,” Sarandos said.As per a Bloomberg report last month, Netflix is still growing at double digits and is on pace for about $15 billion in profit this year.Sarandos, however, was quick to praise the departing staff, emphasising that the cuts were a rare event and not a reflection of their contributions.“And I should mention these are great people who did great work. Unfortunately, it's a very rare occurrence. Obviously, my heart goes out to the folks who were impacted by it, but I think it has made the company healthier for the future,” he added.When asked specifically about the exits of top executives Bela Bajaria and Dan Lin, Sarandos commended their achievements while explaining how leadership needs shift as a business evolves.“Both did a fantastic job for us, and I'm very proud of what they've done. Every once in a while when you're in my seat, you have to look forward and say there's people who are good for the business at one stage who may or may not be good for it at the next stage, and you want to get ahead of that as far as you can,” Sarandos said.Last month, Netflix announced that it would lay off roughly 6% of its employees, or roughly 1,000 workers. The job cuts impacted the product, tech, legal and HR teams.“Our mission - to entertain the world - is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors,” Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters wrote in the email to employees.
Article Summary: Last month, Netflix announced that it would lay off roughly 6% of its employees, or roughly 1,000 workers. The job cuts impacted the product, tech, legal and HR teams. Netflix is still growing at double digits and is on pace for about $15 billion in profit this year.

Article Title: Philips air purifiers claimed to record up to 98.8% PM2.5 reduction in tests at over 2,000 AQI
Article Text:
Philips air purifiers claimed to record up to 98.8% PM2.5 reduction in tests at over 2,000 AQI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Consumer electronics brand Philips has achieved a significant milestone. The company has become India's first air purifier brand to have its products independently evaluated under extreme particulate conditions simulating pollution levels exceeding 2,000 AQI. The evaluation, conducted by FARE Labs, a NABL-accredited testing laboratory, recorded up to 98.8% reduction in PM2.5 levels across the Philips air purifier models tested. The tests commenced at an initial monitor-displayed Air Quality Index (AQI) of 2,361.The evaluation covered seven Philips air purifier models across its portfolio: the Philips 4200 Series, 3200 Series, 2200 Series, 1000 Series, 900 Series, 3400 Series (2-in-1 Air Purifier and Humidifier) and 8000 Series (3-in-1). The tests were conducted in a controlled indoor environment with reference to IS 17531:2021, the Bureau of Indian Standards specification for portable indoor air purifiers. Air quality readings were recorded at approximately 30-second intervals.Among the models evaluated, the Philips 4200 Series recorded a 98.8% reduction in PM2.5, with levels declining from 999 µg/m³ to 12 µg/m³ in approximately 21 minutes.PM10 levels reduced by 97.9%, from 1,999 µg/m³ to 42 µg/m³, while the monitor-displayed AQI decreased from 2,361 to 42. The Philips 3400 Series, a 2-in-1 Air Purifier and Humidifier, recorded a 98.5% reduction in PM2.5, with levels declining from 999 µg/m³ to 15 µg/m³. PM10 levels reduced by 97.9%, from 1,999 µg/m³ to 42 µg/m³, while the monitor-displayed AQI decreased from 2,361 to 42 over approximately 32 minutes. The Philips 900 Series recorded a 97.2% reduction in PM2.5, from 999 µg/m³ to 28 µg/m³, alongside a 96.5% reduction in PM10, from 1,999 µg/m³ to 69 µg/m³. The monitor-displayed AQI fell from 2,361 to 68 over approximately 25 minutes. The other models evaluated, including the Philips 3200 Series, 2200 Series, 1000 Series and 8000 Series (3-in-1), also recorded reductions in airborne particulate levels during their respective testing periods.Gulbahar Taurani, MD & CEO, Versuni India, said: "At Versuni, we believe in turning houses into homes, creating spaces where families feel safe, comfortable and cared for. And the air we breathe plays a vital role in making that possible. As India’s No. 1 Air Purifier Brand, we see this as a responsibility that goes beyond just selling products. India is different. Our pollution levels are different, and so are the homes we live in. That is why we believe our air purifiers must not only meet global standards but also prove their performance under the harsh pollution conditions we face in India. Our recent independent evaluation by FARE Labs, conducted under extremely high particulate pollution conditions at over 2,000 AQI, reinforces this commitment. It marks an important milestone in our journey to establish Philips as India’s first air purifier brand Tested for Indian Conditions."C.S. Joshi, Director, FARE Labs, said: “Testing air purifiers under very high pollution levels helps measure how much airborne particulate matter they can remove under controlled conditions. The results provide useful data on their performance during the test. However, results at home may differ depending on factors such as room size, ventilation and other sources of pollution.”
Article Summary: Consumer electronics brand Philips has achieved a significant milestone. The company has become India's first air purifier brand to have its products independently evaluated under extreme particulate conditions. The evaluation, conducted by FARE Labs, recorded up to 98.8% reduction in PM2.5 levels.

Article Title: Satya Nadella 'admits' Microsoft should have caught Outlook bug before global outage
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft should have caught the software bug that took Outlook offline last week and had safeguards to contain the disruption, chief executive Satya Nadella has said. In an interview with CNBC’s Jim Cramer, Nadella said that the flaw surfaced only under a particular pattern of traffic. “Of course, we should have done the testing before,” he said.The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. Nadella said Microsoft should have designed its systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally.Satya Nadella points to older hardware issueHe also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure. AI tools can help engineers identify software flaws and develop fixes faster, but each fix still has to be tested and installed. More frequent updates, he said, can make existing systems less stable. His comments pointed to a trade-off for software providers as they accelerate the release of patches while keeping widely used services online. "Remember, there is a lot of stuff in our critical infrastructure that’s unpatchable," Nadella said."I mean, think about all the firmware and the chillers [a cooling device often used in data centers] and the HVAC systems everywhere else. So all of that, by the way, they’re on the internet."The interview came a day after Microsoft used its Ignite conference to pitch Copilot as the main interface for work across its business software. A September overhaul brought its AI tools into one app and introduced usage-based charges for more advanced features. Microsoft typically sells workplace software through licences tied to individual employees. Charging for AI usage gives it another source of revenue if customers buy fewer licences. Nadella said usage already accounts for a substantial part of its Dynamics business, which sells software for functions such as sales and enterprise planning.Nadella said Copilot can also direct requests to models from Anthropic, OpenAI or Microsoft itself. The approach gives Microsoft more flexibility over which models it uses in its own products as its relationship with OpenAI evolves.Asked about local opposition to data centre construction, Nadella said that companies had to show residents what they stood to gain. He pointed to Quincy, Washington, where Microsoft has operated a data centre for about two decades, and said tax revenue had helped pay for a school and other public facilities.Nadella also addressed Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia, a major supplier of chips for Microsoft’s Azure cloud. He called Huang a “singular founder” and said that Microsoft remained keen to work with Nvidia’s leadership, including interim chief executive Colette Kress, a former Microsoft employee. He said Nvidia’s board would decide what came next.
Article Summary: Satya Nadella says Microsoft should have designed systems so that a failure in one part of the service could be isolated before it spread globally. The outage disrupted email at businesses that rely on Outlook for day-to-day communication. He also raised a broader problem for companies running older infrastructure.

A large-scale cyberattack exposed visitors to some of the world's most-visited websites to malware after attackers compromised the Optimizely Web experimentation platform, according to security researchers at Report URI. The campaign affected 178 organisations and used trusted website infrastructure to deliver malicious code to unsuspecting users. Researchers said the attackers injected malicious JavaScript into Optimizely customer projects, allowing malware to be served through websites that users would normally consider trustworthy. Because the malicious code was delivered through Optimizely's own content delivery network and security certificates, the attack was difficult to detect.Report URI researcher Scott Helme said the attackers wrote malicious code into customer projects on Optimizely Web, a platform many large companies use to run website experiments. Those sites load a script from Optimizely’s servers, so the malware arrived from a source they already trusted, without their own systems being breached. Helme said it is not known how the attacker gained access to so many unrelated accounts.The malware was designed to perform multiple malicious activities, including stealing cryptocurrency, capturing payment card details, collecting cookies and taking screenshots. For users visiting affected websites on Apple devices, the attackers also deployed the Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits in an apparent attempt to compromise iPhones and iPads. Report URI said cryptocurrency had already been stolen during the campaign, with verified transactions traced to wallets controlled by the attackers.The script swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attacker’s, skimmed card details typed into sites’ own payment forms, and sent back cookies and page screenshots. On iPhones and iPads, it loaded two exploit kits, Coruna and DarkSword, that target older iOS versions. Report URI said iOS 18.7.3 and later, and iOS 26.3 and later, are patched. By 19:25 UTC on Monday, the attacker’s wallets had received about $7,040.Report URI said remediation efforts appeared to be successful, with most of the malicious code removed by the time researchers completed their analysis. The number of infected snippets detected later in the day had fallen sharply compared with earlier findings. The incident highlights the growing risk posed by software supply-chain attacks, where hackers compromise third-party services used by multiple organisations, allowing them to reach large numbers of users without directly attacking each company individually.Most of the malicious code was removed by Monday evening. At 21:52 UTC only TalkTalk’s script was still infected, Report URI said. The firm advised anyone who visited an affected site on Monday to update their iPhone or iPad, check that any crypto transfer went to the intended address, and watch card statements. It said it had not received a response from Optimizely at the time of publication.News & Media (10)Airlines & Travel (9)Crypto & Trading (6)Nonprofit & Civic (4)Gambling (4)Automotive (3)The earlier webshell.lol wave, through Kissmetrics, StorifyMe and Minute Media, affected other sites and isn't included above.
Article Summary: iPhone and iPad users specifically targeted. Most malicious code now removed. Clean-up and advice is now underway. Full list of websites 'infected with malware' is available here. Paychex, Equifax, Hang Seng Investment, MuleSoft and more.

Article Title: Canada faces pushback from Meta, Apple, Alphabet and Signal over Canadian bill that could force them to weaken encryption
Article Text:
Why tech companies are threatening to leave Canada

The ‘fight’ over encryption and ‘backdoors’

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government is reportedly running into fierce resistance from major technology companies over proposed security legislation that would force digital platforms to retain and hand over user data to law enforcement. Executives and lobbyists from Facebook-parent Meta, Apple , and Google-parent Alphabet said to be leading a last-ditch push in Ottawa to rewrite the legislation before it becomes law. Leaders from Meta, Signal Messenger and Tailscale are set to take their objections directly to a key Canadian Senate committee hearing that will shape the bill’s final text, Bloomberg reported.Known as Bill C-22, the “lawful access” legislation is designed to let Canada’s police services and spy agency require electronic service providers to preserve and turn over specific metadata. While the Canadian government argues the rules simply bring the country in line with its Five Eyes and Group of Seven (G7) allies, tech companies, privacy advocates, and US lawmakers contend the bill goes much further – putting user privacy and platform security at risk.Meta has warned that the legislation would effectively turn its platforms into “an arm of the government’s surveillance apparatus.” “There’s a real possibility that both the security and the privacy of Canadian users of these systems is really undermined,” Rachel Curran, Meta’s head of public policy in Canada, said in an interview, the publication reported.For Carney’s government, the standoff carries real economic and diplomatic risks, including chilling tech investment, straining relations with the US and pushing privacy-focused services out of the country altogether. Signal has threatened to pull out of the Canadian market if Bill C-22 passes in its current form while Proton AG, a Swiss tech firm, has said it would reconsider its expansion plans in Canada.Critics take particular issue with a provision allowing authorities to force service providers to store certain user metadata for up to six months in case law enforcement requests it.Bill C-22 could also require certain companies to unlock encrypted data – though only if the company built the encryption itself and holds the keys needed to unlock it. Earlier this year, lawmakers amended the bill to clarify that firms cannot be forced to introduce a “systemic vulnerability” into their software.Those safeguards were meant to reassure companies like Signal and Meta (which owns WhatsApp) that end-to-end encryption wouldn’t be targeted. Because end-to-end encryption ensures only the sender and recipient can read a message, the companies themselves have no way to decrypt the content.Still, privacy groups and tech leaders argue the bill leaves the government with broad authority to order firms to build “technical capabilities” to intercept communications and hand over data. Tech companies have consistently maintained that they cannot build a law enforcement “backdoor” without weakening security for everyone.Curran called any order that weakens Meta’s systems a “red line” for the company and likely its peers. “It probably puts Canada in a position where there’s going to eventually be a bit of a standoff between service providers and the government, and it’s not good for Canadians,” she added.Meanwhile, Canada’s public safety minister Gary Anandasangaree has maintained that Bill C-22 was already revised to address the encryption concerns, accusing Big Tech critics of spreading misinformation.“Bill C-22 does not authorise indiscriminate surveillance and does not permit or compel companies to introduce systemic vulnerabilities or so-called ‘backdoors.’ Any claims suggesting otherwise are incorrect,” said Simon Lafortune, the minister’s spokesperson, in a statement.Apple has acknowledged the government’s efforts to improve the draft, but said the current bill would still hurt its ability to protect users with encryption and privacy tools, “even as AI and other evolving technologies provide hackers with new tools to exploit cybersecurity weaknesses.”
Article Summary: Canadian government running into fierce resistance over proposed security legislation. Bill C-22 would force digital platforms to retain and hand over user data to law enforcement. Meta, Signal Messenger and Tailscale are set to take their objections directly to a key Canadian Senate committee hearing that will shape the bill’s final text.

Article Title: US government's Department of Commerce and Department of Justice ‘break rule’, issue joint statement on MegaSpeed, the company at 'centre' of Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's 'romantic scandal'
Article Text:
Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice's joint statement on investigation into Singaporean company Megaspeed

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For the first time, two US government departments -- US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice -- have issued a joint statement on MegaSpeed, the Singapore-based company caught in Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's scandal. The statement makes it clear what made the two departments break the rule of not commenting on and ongoing investigations. The statement says, "While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting."For those unaware, the Singapore-based cloud computing company MegaSpeed has faced heightened scrutiny since former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said that he had been unfaithful to his wife following reports linking him to former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia on November 12 amid fallout from reports about his extramarital relationships, one of which was reportedly a direct reportee.On its website, Megaspeed describes itself as a "core business partner" of Nvidia’s computing power cloud business in the region. It enables customers to rent computing power from Nvidia GPUs. The company has offices in Singapore and Indonesia.The Department of Commerce and the Department of Justice are providing the public with an update on the investigation of the Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has attracted significant public attention in the last week.While we don’t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting.After identifying suspicious activity through proactive monitoring of potential sensitive semiconductor diversion, the Department of Commerce initiated an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export control violations. In May 2025, Department of Commerce investigators requested records from Nvidia concerning direct or indirect sales to Megaspeed. In June 2025, Nvidia placed Megaspeed on its “no sell” list. Based on the Department of Commerce’s investigation, agents from the Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security, in conjunction with Singaporean law enforcement officials, conducted an on-site, in-person, end-use check at Megaspeed in June 2025 and interviewed CEO Alice Huang.Following this enforcement action, the Department of Justice took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed.The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce’s Bureau of Industry and Security working together will bring the full extent of the law against Megaspeed for any criminal conduct that may have occurred. This investigation is the result of the excellent work of the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick and the law enforcement efforts of the Department of Justice under Attorney General Todd Blanche.The Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce have an extremely strong track record of bringing semiconductor smugglers to justice. Under the Trump Administration, seventeen defendants across six separate investigations have been charged in connection with allegations of smuggling billions of dollars’ worth of semiconductors. Furthermore, the Department of Commerce has brought monetary penalties to new highs across export control cases, representing an eighteen-fold increase over the Biden administration.Sensitive technologies like semiconductors are among the most valuable and strategic assets of the U.S. economy, and the Department of Justice and the Department of Commerce will remain vigilant in pursuing justice for those who want to compromise America’s technological edge.
Article Summary: US Department of Commerce and Department of Justice have issued a joint statement on MegaSpeed, the Singapore-based company caught in Nvidia founder Jensen Huang's scandal. EY India has announced the sixth cohort of its Executive Program on Board Effectiveness, aimed at equipping current directors and senior executives with the skills needed to navigate evolving boardroom responsibilities, including oversight of artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity and corporate governance. The four-week programme will commence on 19 November 2026 and is designed for existing board members as well as senior leaders aspiring to take up board positions. According to EY India, the initiative seeks to strengthen participants' strategic judgment, financial oversight and governance capabilities as expectations from corporate boards continue to expand beyond traditional compliance functions.EY India highlighted that directors are increasingly expected to contribute to strategy formation, risk governance, technology oversight, financial resilience and long-term value creation, rather than serving solely as compliance watchdogs. The firm cited findings from the ISB Corporate Governance Report 2025, which surveyed more than 200 directors from BSE 500 companies. While 98% of respondents said their boards were compliant with governance requirements, only 17% reported that their boards actively shaped company strategy. A further 36% said their boards had limited or no involvement beyond reviewing management plans.Commenting on the programme, Aashish Kasad, Partner and India Region Diversity & Inclusiveness Business Sponsor at EY India, said the transition from executive leadership to the boardroom requires a shift from operating a business to challenging, guiding and overseeing it."Directors need to connect strategy with financial resilience, governance and deliberate on organisation readiness on topical matters such as impact of AI and cybersecurity, while exercising independent judgment," Kasad said, adding that the programme is intended to help leaders contribute to boards with greater clarity and confidence.The Executive Program on Board Effectiveness includes more than 40 hours of learning across nine sessions. Topics covered include board leadership and effectiveness, directors' responsibilities, board committees, environmental, social and governance (ESG) issues, financial statement interpretation, AI and cybersecurity, board recruitment and emerging governance challenges. Participants will also engage in governance case studies, simulated board and committee discussions, and scenario-based exercises designed to enhance strategic contribution, risk awareness, stakeholder stewardship, integrity and ethical decision-making.Originally introduced as a platform for senior women leaders, the programme has now been expanded to a broader leadership audience. EY India said it plans to offer two cohorts each year, enabling more professionals to prepare for boardroom responsibilities and benefit from peer learning opportunities. The programme is targeted at CXO-level executives seeking board positions, senior leaders from corporate, public and non-profit organisations, investor representatives serving on boards, leaders from multinational companies and Indian subsidiaries, as well as existing directors looking to strengthen their effectiveness in a rapidly changing governance environment.

Article Title: Microsoft 365 outage: Company blames a 'triple' failure for 24-hour-plus global Outlook disruption; Microsoft EVP Charles Lamanna says: Three main factors that...
Article Text:
Microsoft explains its global outage

A July bug slipped past Microsoft 365's load testing

A Teams failover and 14% missing capacity exposed the bug

Outlook stayed down longest because Exchange Online could not switch gateways

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft has explained what disrupted Outlook, Exchange Online and a string of other Microsoft 365 services for more than 24 hours last week, and the answer is not one fault but three. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up on November 12. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive at the worst point.Charles Lamanna, Microsoft's executive vice president for Copilot, Agents and Platform, detailed the root cause of the Microsoft 365 outage in a post on X on Monday. "The incident on Thursday, November 12th, 2026, was caused by three main factors that together caused a global outage for the networking gateway that fronts many Microsoft 365 services," he wrote. He also apologised: "We are deeply sorry for the impact to all our customers and recognize the impact that this has on their normal business & operations. "The first factor was a latent defect. Under certain load conditions, lock contention inside an internal process left servers overwhelmed and unresponsive.The bug came from a fix built specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers. Lamanna said neither the defect nor that fix applies to broader Windows deployments.The change began rolling out in July, cleared safe deployment, reached servers worldwide over several weeks and ran for more than three months without trouble.So why did testing miss it? Microsoft's load tests leaned on its weaker hardware with fewer cores, while the contention problem gets worse on newer machines with more cores. The test labs' traffic and hardware mix did not match the live fleet.Microsoft runs two independent network gateway systems inside Microsoft 365, so services can move between them during disruptions. About 15 hours before the outage, Teams failed over from the alternative gateway to the "primary" one, which also handles Exchange Online. The company calls this routine, but it added load and changed traffic patterns on that gateway.At the same time, nearly 14% of the gateway's server capacity was out of service because of an unrelated issue from the day before. That alone caused no harm, since the service had enough headroom.Together, though, the extra load and thinner capacity triggered the July bug during peak US traffic hours. Requests piled up until servers stopped responding. Microsoft's traffic management then moved users to healthy endpoints, as designed, which simply spread the same load across fewer machines. In under two hours, the defect had hit servers across the fleet.A separate issue meant the bulkheads between regional "capacity units" also failed to contain the damage, letting a gateway problem become a global outage.Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint and Office apps could move off the faulty infrastructure, which is why they came back sooner. Teams chats and meetings worked for most of the outage. Exchange Online, which powers Outlook email, could not make that switch.Recovery was a fight of its own. Servers returning to service were flooded by queued traffic and went down again. Microsoft's automated recovery systems were not designed for such a broad failure, and because the bug was months old, the usual rollback, flighting and feature flag tools could not quickly reverse it. Even the company's status updates during the outage said it had "not identified any recent change correlated with the start of impact.Engineers eventually built an update that returned the code path to its last known good state. They then pulled groups of servers out of service, applied the fix and restarted them, in some cases more than half a region at a time.Microsoft first flagged the problem at 11:24 pm IST on November 12, for users in the Americas, before it spread to at least 70 countries and hit Copilot, government offices, courts and hospitals. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air reported problems with their customer-support email systems, while OpenAI and Anthropic flagged issues with their Microsoft 365 integrations. The Microsoft executive had already ruled out foul play on November 13, writing, "This was not a cyberattack or an issue caused by AI tooling. "A final Post-Incident Review (PIR) is due later this week. It should also shed light on the separate issue that let the failure jump across regions, which Monday's summary leaves unexplained.
Article Summary: Microsoft 365 went down for more than 24 hours on November 12. A software bug that had sat unnoticed on its servers since July, a sudden rise in traffic and a chunk of server capacity already offline all lined up. The result was a chain reaction that left more than 80% of the servers behind a key Microsoft 365 networking gateway unresponsive.

Article Title: As cyberattack hits European Commission, FBI's AI tool warning in focus
Article Text:
EU Commission hit by cyberattack

How hackers targeted the Commission with an AI tool

Over 10 days of workplace disruption

Crisis response reaches the highest levels

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A major cyberattack has hit the European Commission, potentially exposing large amounts of personal data, locking staff out of critical human resources systems for more than 10 days, a report has said, adding that the incident has also forced top officials to address the crisis during their weekly meeting on Wednesday (November 18). While the Commission believes it has contained most of the breach, investigators are still working to determine the full scope of the damage.“The systems may be coming back online. The answers are taking a little longer,” said an EU official, speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, as per a report in Politico.Earlier this month, CERT-EU, the cybersecurity watchdog for EU institutions, discovered that international hackers were using ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool built to spot weaknesses in IT systems. The EU official said: “Some actors misuse such tools and have targeted the Commission.”In response, the Commission temporarily pulled several applications offline as a precaution, though access to most of them has since been restored. Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed that “individual systems were targeted” in a detected cyber campaign and noted that affected parties have been notified in line with standard practice.However, investigators still do not know whether staff data was stolen or how widespread any leak might be. According to the anonymous EU official, this lingering uncertainty is the reason employees have received limited updates so far.The report comes soon after the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned in a FLASH advisory that hackers are using ARTEX, an open-source, large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous penetration testing framework, to automate multiple stages of cyber intrusions. The agency also said hackers have used the tool since at least August to target organisations across financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications and legal sectors.The cyber incident has caused major day-to-day headaches for Commission employees for more than a week and a half, leaving staff unable to enter salary and leave details:HR and medical platforms: Sysper, which is the Commission's internal HR hub for payslips, leave requests and timesheets, and MyPMO, its medical reimbursement system, were brought back online earlier this week, though Sysper suffered another brief crash.Translation services: Translation tools were also disrupted this week, prompting one frustrated official to admit to “swearing a lot”, Politico reported.The severity of the breach prompted action from the Commission's top leadership. According to a leaked internal email viewed by Playbook (Politico), the Corporate Management Board (the institution's highest internal crisis-management group) held an urgent meeting earlier this month to address the “ongoing cyber incidents.”At the same time, the digital services department rolled out stricter security checks, and Tech Commissioner Henna Virkkunen updated fellow officials on the immediate response during Wednesday's College of Commissioners meeting, two officials confirmed.
Article Summary: European Commission believes it has contained most of the breach. However, investigators are still working to determine the full scope of the damage. Hackers were using ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool built to spot weaknesses in IT systems. Commission temporarily pulled several applications offline as a precaution.

Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg

What the lawsuit says about Instagram and child safety

How Matt Eisner links the allegations to Meta’s costs

Meta shareholder Matt Eisner has sued Mark Zuckerberg . In a 656-page complaint lawsuit in federal court in Northern California this week, he named the Meta CEO and 25 others, including executives and board members. Eisner alleges that the leaders of Facebook and Instagram ’s parent company prioritised keeping users active on its platforms over protecting children and teenagers.According to a Forbes report, the complaint alleges that Meta’s leaders crafted a public account “designed to mask a systemic crisis in user engagement and growth.” Eisner says their assurances about child safety inflated Meta’s stock price, causing the company to pay more than it should have when it bought back its own shares. He filed a shareholder derivative suit seeking to recover money for Meta on the company’s behalf. Meta is named as a nominal defendant.The complaint says Meta described its recommendation system as fostering “meaningful interaction” while, Eisner alleges, “it was engineered to reward toxicity for engagement.” It also calls Meta’s 2024 proxy statement, which gives investors information ahead of shareholder votes, “materially false and misleading.” Eisner alleges that the filing misstated how Meta protected children and omitted risks the company faced if those measures fell short.ForbesInstagram head Adam Mosseri is also named in the lawsuit, which claims he prioritised “‘clicks’ over child welfare.” It says Mosseri made hiding likes optional to protect engagement, while studies show hiding counts reduced harmful social comparison.Meta’s financial filings show that it spent $25.63 billion buying back shares in the nine months through September 2021 and $26.26 billion on buybacks in 2025, including excise taxes. Those figures represent total repurchase costs. Eisner alleges that Meta overpaid because misleading statements had inflated the share price. He also points to Meta’s August 2026 agreement with 52 attorneys general to resolve litigation over teen mental health and social media. Meta says the agreement provides for payments of up to about $18.59 billion.In 2024, US District Judge Charles Breyer dismissed Eisner’s earlier case against Meta and Zuckerberg after finding that the complaint failed to adequately connect the alleged disclosure failures to an economic loss. In the new case, Eisner is asking the court to require corrective disclosures and block Meta from holding a shareholder meeting until investors receive them. 2024 dismissal order, the report noted.

Article Title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has a warning about what happens when AI replaces human workers: If there’s only capital and there’s no labor, I don’t know..
Article Text:
Satya Nadella: AI without workers is “not an economy”

One AI model could run healthcare, finance and even government, says Nadella

Nadella wants every company to build its own “token capital”

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has warned that if AI replaces human workers at scale, the damage won’t stop at jobs and could reach the ballot box. Speaking at a roundtable after his Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote at San Francisco’s Chase Center, Nadella said an economy run entirely on AI would leave democracy with nothing to stand on.“No one, at least in a democracy, can even win an election if this just goes that way, if there’s only capital and there’s no labor,” Nadella said, according to The Verge. “I mean, I don’t know, that’s not an economy.”He was answering a question about Anthropic adding more products to its office suite, where Microsoft has been strongest for decades. He didn’t talk about competing products at all. Instead he raised a bigger fear, which is one AI company owning everything. “If the Marxist sort of view is that there’s only one firm, then it’s over, right? For all of us,” he said. He added that even the reporters in the room would “somehow be some affiliate of Anthropic. ”Nadella rejected the idea that AI is just a race among tech giants for the next trillion dollars in market value. He called it “one of the strangest, narrowest ways” to think about it. A model has no natural limits, he argued. It could become a healthcare company or a financial services firm, and “it can take over the government.”That raises the question of what companies are even for. If a model learns from everything it sees and “all of human capital collapses into token capital,” Nadella asked, what role is left for a firm and the people who work there?Nadella told The Verge that he is now “AGI-pilled,” mainly when it comes to how AI could rewire the economy and politics. That doesn’t go as far as consciousness. Asked whether models like Anthropic’s Claude are conscious, he said, “I don’t think so.” That puts him on the same side as Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman, who argues AI shouldn’t be treated as having moral status. Nadella was less firm about it than Suleyman, though, and called it “a good debate. ”Nadella first made this argument in a June post on X. There, he said every company needs “token capital,” the AI capability it owns, alongside the human capital of its employees. He also argued that human capital gets more valuable as token capital grows. If a few models capture all the value, he wrote, “the political economy will simply not tolerate it.” He compared that risk to the way outsourcing hollowed out industrial economies during globalisation.Microsoft’s Ignite announcements follow the same idea. The new tools let businesses pick cost-effective AI models, run their own models and keep control of their data. “If you believe that the world, the economy needs more than one firm or two firms, then by definition there need to be as many models as firms of some sort,” Nadella said.The timing stands out. Anthropic, which counts Microsoft among its investors, is expected to start trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on Thursday. Nadella’s argument is that if the AI economy leaves workers with no stake in it, voters will stop backing it.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella: AI without workers is “not an economy’ One AI model could run healthcare, finance and even government, says Nadeella. He wants every company to build its own “token capital’

Article Title: Rising tech outages put digital resilience in focus
Article Text:
Representative image

Widespread disruption

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Bengaluru: Another day, another major technology outage. Over the past week, disruptions have hit Microsoft Outlook and Teams, Cloudflare, AWS, Anthropic's Claude, Workday, Apple services, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), United Airlines, JPMorgan Chase and even the US National Security Agency's classified network, NSANet.In India, a Microsoft cloud outage disrupted email-based customer support at IndiGo, Air India and Akasa Air, while financial services, telecom and IT companies reported problems accessing corporate email and workplace applications. Flight operations were unaffected.Cloudflare also reported disruptions at multiple Indian locations earlier this month. Apple blamed Tuesday's outages on an internal update, ruling out a cyberattack. The disruptions affected the App Store, iCloud sign-in, mail and web apps, with some services down for over four hours. While consumer services were restored by Wednesday, two outages affecting its developer platform, App Store Connect, remained listed."The most alarming thing about this wave of outages is how a failure in one part of our digital infrastructure can disrupt airlines, banks, governments, and millions of people almost simultaneously," said Tal Kollender, founder and CEO of Israeli cybersecurity firm Remedio.A single misconfiguration, failed update or broken dependency can trigger widespread disruption, she said. As AI becomes embedded in critical infrastructure, autonomous systems making decisions and changes at speeds humans cannot always control could add to the risks. Cybersecurity must move beyond detecting problems to fixing vulnerabilities, with safeguards to ensure corrective actions do not cause further outages, she added.Diwakar Dayal, managing director and area vice-president, SentinelOne India and SAARC, said the biggest cyber risk was not just a breach but the inability to operate when technology failed."Digital resilience is becoming a new measure of business leadership. In an interconnected world, a technology failure anywhere can become a business crisis everywhere," he said.For India, where digital infrastructure underpins banking, aviation, public services and commerce, resilience was an economic and national security imperative. Companies need operational redundancy and the ability to contain disruption and recover quickly, he added. Rahul Sasi, CEO and co-founder of CloudSEK, said even unsuccessful cyber exploitation attempts could disrupt services.

Article Title: Billionaire Bill Ackman criticises Nvidia board for Jensen Huang's removal, says it is compounding its failures by…
Article Text:
Bill Ackman targets Nvidia board over Jensen Huang's removal

Bill Ackman accuses of rushed decisions

Ackman says Nvidia's board is ‘compounding its failures’

Read Bill Ackman’s full post

I believe the @nvidia board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders nor in a manner consistent with their fiduciary duties.

What we know is that the board fired

Jensen

or forced his resignation for violating company policy and/or in response to the accusation of an affair with a spy.

They did so without careful consideration of the impact on the company, its customers, its shareholders or other stakeholders.

They rushed to judgment without the benefit of careful due diligence or even with a basic understanding of the facts.

How do we know this?

We know this by how quickly Jensen was fired and how little was known at the time of his firing.

It takes time to convene a board meeting. There was time, maybe, for one Zoom.

And this is a decision that should have been made by a board sitting in person and carefully deliberating the facts once they are known.

And they should have slept on the decision and met again the day after to discuss the facts, the risks and the other implications of their decision.

The timing and lack of information did not allow for careful board deliberation.

While boards can fire a CEO for an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, it should not be an automatic decision.

That is why we have boards comprised of humans and not agents.

A board should consider whether or not such a relationship was consensual or whether it was an abuse of power dynamics. And a board has to consider what the impact of the firing is on all stakeholders.

If I were in this board, I would not have rushed to judgment based on articles in the media. I would have made sure the board had all of the facts so it could make a careful and informed decision.

Boards of Delaware companies have a duty of care which means they must make informed, prudent and good faith decisions. This clearly did not happen here.

What law firm is advising this board?

Or is the board even taken good legal advice?

It doesn’t look like it.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

And now the board is compounding its failures by insisting that there is no possibility for Jensen’s return as CEO.

Why is it in the best interest of the company to foreclose the possibility of Jensen’s return and to do so before all of the facts are known? This is yet another breach of their duty of care.

Furthermore, the board has launched an investigation whose scope is unknown. Investigations can be extremely damaging to a company and should be carefully targeted to address whatever facts need to be known rather than be overly broad in scope.

In short, this looks like a series of major governance failures by directors that panicked due to headlines in the media. They likely felt compelled to do something because they were afraid of looking bad in the media, not because it was the right thing for them company.

They couldn’t stand the heat.

The board’s conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history.

Billionaire investor Bill Ackman has sharply criticised Nvidia’s board of directors over the removal of CEO Jensen Huang, accusing them of panicking over media headlines and failing in their legal duties to shareholders. In a pointed critique posted on X (formerly Twitter), Ackman argued that the board is not acting in the best interest of shareholders or fulfilling its responsibilities. According to Ackman, the directors either fired Huang or forced his resignation over a company policy violation and/or accusations of an affair with a spy – and did so without carefully weighing how the move would affect the company, its customers, shareholders, or other stakeholders.Ackman contends that the speed of Huang’s exit proves the board rushed to judgment without conducting proper due diligence or even having a basic grasp of the facts.While acknowledging that a board has the authority to fire a CEO over an inappropriate relationship with a subordinate, Ackman stressed that it should never be an automatic knee-jerk reaction. He added that directors should evaluate whether a relationship was consensual or an abuse of power, alongside the broader fallout for everyone tied to the company.Beyond the initial ouster, Ackman warned that the board is making matters worse by ruling out any chance of bringing Huang back as CEO – all before a full set of facts has even been established. He also raised concerns over an internal investigation launched by the board, noting that its scope remains unknown.
Article Summary: Billionaire investor Bill Ackman has sharply criticised Nvidia’s board of directors over the removal of CEO Jensen Huang. Ackman accuses them of panicking over media headlines and failing in their legal duties to shareholders. According to Ackman, the directors either fired Huang or forced his resignation over a company policy violation.

Article Title: FAA goes back to this 25-year-old Cisco tech after network crash that hit 15,000 US flights and stranded 1.5 million passengers
Article Text:
Representative image

US officials give different explanations

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has stopped installing new routers linked to last week’s nationwide ground stop and has switched off the ones already running. That essentially puts the US air traffic system back on Cisco routers that have been in place for about 25 years. Notably, the agency still has not said what caused the failure. An FAA spokesperson confirmed the halt on the Juniper Networks routers to ABC News. The spokesperson added that the agency “has not yet determined the root cause of Friday’s issue.” As per a separate report, the FAA had also turned off the Juniper units already installed. It is now relying on the older Cisco gear to keep the network running while it investigates.The development comes days after the ground stop lasted more than four hours, the longest nationwide ground stop since the September 11 attacks. According to ABC News, more than 14,000 flights were cancelled on Friday and Saturday (November 14 and 15). Radar feeds and aircraft communications were disrupted at 17 of the FAA’s 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The agency says “excessive data” flooded its telecommunications network at a rate of 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds.That overwhelmed legacy equipment, according to the AP.The retreat from the new routers came a day after the Trump administration offered a very different theory. On November 16, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said, “I believe that it’s the SI (superintelligence).” Mullin said he was relaying a theory from an unnamed tech-industry contact. The idea is that self-coding, self-fixing programs could overwhelm systems that cannot keep pace. In the same interview, he said he could tell Americans “with 98% certainty, we’re not seeing a cyber attack. ”Meanwhile, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that the cause was either “contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment.” He also said the FAA’s new AI air-traffic tool, SMART, played no role. The $875 million system was expanded to the airspace of all 22 centres on Nov. 10, three days before the outage, the AP reported.FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said at a press conference: “We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related.”Delta CEO Ed Bastian told Fortune at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit that the ground stop came from “a combination of faulty equipment, coupled with human error.” He said there is no evidence of an AI trigger or a cyber attack.Pulling the routers does not close the case. Thirteen Democrats on the Senate Commerce Committee, including ranking member Maria Cantwell and Sen. Ben Ray Luján, wrote to Duffy in a letter released Tuesday. They asked him to keep the pause in place until the root cause is found.“Identifying the device that failed does not establish why it failed,” they wrote. Citing L3Harris, the letter says 3,648 routers are due to be converted to Juniper devices. About 400 have been installed, and 69 are operational.
Article Summary: US air traffic system back on Cisco routers that have been in place for about 25 years. More than 14,000 flights were cancelled on Friday and Saturday (November 14 and 15) Radar feeds and aircraft communications were disrupted at 17 of the FAA’s 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

Article Title: Anthropic filing reveals how much company stake Amazon and Google will own

Breaking down the Amazon and Google stakes in Anthropic

Two of Anthropic’s largest customers, Amazon and Alphabet’s Google, will hold more than 28% of the artificial intelligence (AI) startup’s stock combined once it goes public. According to a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), Amazon is set to own nearly 15% of Anthropic’s outstanding capital stock, while Google will hold nearly 14% following the initial public offering (IPO) and a concurrent private placement.The regulatory filing offers a closer look at how those shares are structured:Google will hold 1.79 billion shares, accounting for 32% of the Claude chatbot maker’s non-voting stock after the IPO. This includes 135.1 million non-voting shares that Google agreed to purchase for roughly $10 billion as part of a $26 billion private placement arranged alongside the public offering, Bloomberg reported.Amazon will own 1.92 billion non-voting shares, representing 34% of Anthropic's Class N stock. While Amazon’s total stake could reach 24% if it converted all of its outstanding notes and waived its ownership cap, the e-commerce giant has agreed not to waive that limit. Under their agreement, Amazon will only exercise convertible notes if doing so keeps its overall stake at or below 12%.Anthropic and its co-founders are looking to raise up to $64.4 billion through the IPO.When combined with the $26 billion private placement, the deal would become the largest first-time share sale in history, topping SpaceX’s $75 billion base deal from June.Bloomberg says investor appetite for the offering has been high, with orders reaching nearly seven times the number of available shares. Citing people familiar with the matter, the report says that bankers have informed prospective investors that existing backers will get priority, meaning some new buyers will likely receive smaller share allocations than they hoped for.The IPO is scheduled to price on Wednesday, November 18.The filing also highlights the overlapping roles that tech giants play in Anthropic’s business. In the document, Anthropic states that Amazon, Google and Microsoft “simultaneously serve as our investors, customers, distribution partners, and competitors.” Through their cloud platforms, Amazon, Google, and Microsoft allow their customers to buy access to Anthropic’s Claude AI models using existing cloud accounts.

The department said that Waymo cars will be barred from freeways from November 11. It "will remain in place until Waymo demonstrates to the department that it has taken effective corrective actions," DMV said.As mentioned above, the ban follows a viral video dated November 6 that showed a Waymo robotaxi attempting to pass a CHP⁠ cruiser with its lights on controlling traffic on Interstate 280 in San Francisco. In its email, the DMV mentioned this incident along with another where a Waymo entered an active construction closure on Highway 101 near Burlingame."The department determined that Waymo’s driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present, despite a prior restriction and corrective actions implemented following similar incidents," the DMV stated.Notably, this is not the first time that Waymo has been banned on freeway. Waymo was shut out from freeway rides in May because of issues involving construction zones."Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on U.S. 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state," a Waymo spokesperson said in an email to the publication."In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. ""Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week," the statement continued. "We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations."
Article Summary: The California Department of Motor Vehicles has banned Waymo robotaxis from freeway driving indefinitely. The move comes after a viral video showed a robotaxi failing to yield to a California Highway Patrol officer in the Bay Area. The department said that Waymo cars will be barred from freeways from November 11.

Article Title: As Anthropic's IPO is less than 24 hours away, here's Blackstone's 'junk warning' to investors
Article Text:
Anthropic’s leaked IPO filing reveals soaring revenue, massive infrastructure costs, customer concentration and the financial risks behind its AI ambitions.

What a junk rating could mean for Anthropic

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Where Blackstone has money at stake

Anthropic is expected to go public on November 19. The Claude maker plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Its latest US filing sets an expected price range of $70 to $78 a share, putting the total offering at about $61 billion at the midpoint. However, Blackstone has reportedly warned its investors about buying shares of the AI companyA Financial Times report citing people familiar with the matter claims Blackstone has told its investors that Anthropic could receive a “high” junk credit rating after its IPO due to the AI company’s $63 billion chip financing deal. The private capital firm had previously expected Anthropic to reach investment grade by year-end. A rating in the BB range would put Anthropic near the top of the speculative-grade category and could make it more expensive to borrow for computing infrastructure.A below-investment-grade rating could narrow Anthropic’s pool of lenders. Some insurers and pension funds face limits on how much lower-rated debt they can hold, and lenders generally demand higher yields from borrowers they consider riskier. The FT reported that Anthropic outlined plans to spend more than $800 billion on computing infrastructure through 2045.The rating also matters for Anthropic’s existing credit facility. Its offering documents say the company can elect to have guarantees and collateral released if it obtains investment-grade ratings from at least two of Moody’s, S&P and Fitch and meets other conditions. FT noted that none of those three agencies had issued a rating for Anthropic when its report was released last month.The chip financing, known as Project North Star, lets Anthropic lease 1.5 gigawatts of Google-designed chips. Broadcom, which co-develops the chips and has an investment-grade rating, guarantees more than $42 billion of senior loans.Another $18 billion in junior debt is backed by Anthropic’s lease payments and ranks behind the senior loans for repayment in a default. Blackstone’s funds invested $9 billion in the junior debt at a yield above 10%, the FT reported.
Article Summary: Anthropic is expected to go public on November 19. The AI maker plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. Its latest US filing sets an expected price range of $70 to $78 a share. Blackstone has reportedly warned its investors about buying shares of the AI company.

Sharp contrast with Jensen Huang’s stance

China sales come to an end: Colette Kress, Nvidia CEO

Nvidia board focuses on national security

Nvidia’s approach to China appears to be undergoing a significant change after the departure of founder Jensen Huang, who had spent years lobbying for greater access to the Chinese market. According to a report by Bloomberg, Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress has said that the company is no longer shipping licensed Hopper datacenter chips to China and does not expect such sales to contribute to future results. Speaking during the latest earnings call of the company, Kress stated that the AI chip giant sold around $2.4 billion worth of licensed Hopper datacenter products in China during the third quarter. However, she added that the company’s future guidance does not include any licensed Hopper datacenter products and also confirmed that Nvidia has stopped shipping those products to Chinese customers.This move of Nvidia marks a notable departure from the position championed by Jensen Huang, who had repeatedly argued for maintaining access to the Chinese market and sought US government approval to sell advanced AI processors there.As per the Bloomberg report, Nvidia earlier pushed Washington for permission to sell its Blackwell AI chips to China. While, the Trump administration did not approve those requests, it later permitted the sales of Hopper-based H200 processors, which are older than Nvidia's latest Rubin-generation products. For the uninitiated, Huang has been one of the most vocal advocates for exports to China, frequently emphasising the importance of the market to Nvidia’s long-term growth strategy.Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress has not explained the reason as to why the company is ending shipments to China, but her comments does indicate that Nvidia is stepping away from a business that generated billions of dollars in recent revenue. The announcement also comes at a time when the US government tightens restrictions on advanced AI chip exports. Recently, the Trump administration also introduced measures which are directed towards increasing scrutiny of processor exports and limiting sales to overseas data centers that could offer Chinese companies with remote access to advanced AI infrastructure.The report also adds that the shift in Nvidia’s stance also reflects growing concerns around national security and export controls. Harvey Jones, who was appointed Nvidia's first board chair last week, said the company recognises that changing national security dynamics are having a major impact on the market. "The company's next CEO will need to navigate those waters very carefully," Jones said, according to Bloomberg.Nvidia also announced the creation of a dedicated board-level committee focused on national security and export-control issues, signalling that geopolitical considerations are likely to play a larger role in future business decisions.Despite Nvidia's leadership turmoil, Nadella expressed confidence in the company's management team and long-term prospects. "Nvidia does have a lot of human capital and very capable leadership," he said, highlighting interim CEO and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who previously worked at Microsoft.Nadella also stressed the importance of Microsoft's ongoing relationship with the chipmaker, noting that the company is continuing to scale deployment of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin processors. "I'm making sure that we have the same type of partnership, and we're scaling Rubins as we speak," Nadella said. "It's a pretty critical project for us."Microsoft is one of Nvidia's largest customers, purchasing vast quantities of AI accelerators for its cloud infrastructure. The two companies have maintained a close partnership during the AI boom, with Nadella and Huang frequently appearing together at industry events.
Article Summary: N Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper datacenter chips to China. Colette Kress, interim CEO, said the company does not expect such sales to contribute to future results. This marks a notable departure from the position championed by Jensen Huang, who had repeatedly argued for maintaining access to the Chinese market. The shift in Nvidia’s stance also reflects growing concerns around national security and export controls.

Anduril founder Palmer Luckey

NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani

What is Mamdani’s pied-à-terre tax and which properties are covered

Why Sergey Brin 'exited' New York City

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani recently shared an update on the pied-à-terre surcharge, popularly called as 'house tax'. In a post on X (formerly known as Twitter), Zohran Mamdani said that the city has billed over $500 million to rich owners of second homes. “That’s half a billion dollars to invest in a City that works for all New Yorkers,” Mamdani wrote. Introduced earlier this year, the pied-à-terre tax apples to homes worth over $5 million that are not the owner’s main residence. Among those impacted by the tax includes Google founder Sergey Brin , Amazon founder Jeff Bezos and Dell CEO Michael Dell. A Bloomberg report in July said that Sergey Brin walked away from a sizable bet on New York City apartment, selling his stake in a struggling real estate fund for just six cents on the dollar.Sharing the X post, Zohran Mamdani wrote:“An update on our pied-à-terre surcharge: We’ve billed more than $500 million to owners of second homes worth more than $5 million. That’s half a billion dollars to invest in a City that works for all New Yorkers”.As mentioned above, the new pied-à-terre tax is a surcharge on houses that are not the primary residence of owners. It applies to one-, two- and three-family homes valued at more than $5 million, as well as condominiums and co-ops valued at $1 million or more, if those properties are not a person's primary residence.The measure is intended primarily to cover owners who maintain homes in New York City while living elsewhere for most of the year and therefore do not pay New York City income taxes.According to a Bloomberg report, Google founder Sergey Brin offloaded his sizable holding in a New York City apartment back to the fund's manager, A&E Real Estate. Amphitheatre LLC, an entity tied to Brin, sold its shares in a fund holding nearly 5,900 units across Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens and the Bronx, the report stated. Many of those apartments fall under New York's rent-stabilization program.A&E then confirmed the buyout without naming Brin, saying the investor "was willing to accept six cents on the dollar on their original equity investment to divest itself from the New York City multifamily sector.”

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has expressed his admiration for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after his departure from the AI chip giant, but he also made it clear that any decision about the return of Huang is not his to make. According to a report Fortune, speaking at a media roundtable during Microsoft’s Ignite conference in San Francisco, Nadella described Huang as ‘a singular person’ who has made some significant contributions to both Nvidia and the broader technology industry. However, he stopped short of endorsing a potential comeback for the Nvidia co-founder. "I just want to give him space for what he needs to do there, and it's not up to me. It's up to the Nvidia board to decide what happens next," Nadella said. He added that he has "all the admiration, respect for what Jensen has done for this industry, and what he's done for Nvidia," noting that the two have worked together for many years.Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO last week amid controversy surrounding revelations about his personal life. The long-time executive, who co-founded Nvidia more than three decades ago and helped transform it into the world's leading AI chipmaker, later said he would be willing to return as CEO if given the opportunity.However, Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones subsequently indicated that the company had no plans to bring Huang back to the top role, leaving uncertainty around the executive's future.Despite Nvidia's leadership turmoil, Nadella expressed confidence in the company's management team and long-term prospects. "Nvidia does have a lot of human capital and very capable leadership," he said, highlighting interim CEO and Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, who previously worked at Microsoft.Nadella also stressed the importance of Microsoft's ongoing relationship with the chipmaker, noting that the company is continuing to scale deployment of Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin processors. "I'm making sure that we have the same type of partnership, and we're scaling Rubins as we speak," Nadella said. "It's a pretty critical project for us."Microsoft is one of Nvidia's largest customers, purchasing vast quantities of AI accelerators for its cloud infrastructure. The two companies have maintained a close partnership during the AI boom, with Nadella and Huang frequently appearing together at industry events.During the discussion, Nadella also commented on growing opposition to data centre developments across parts of the United States. He said technology companies must earn public trust by demonstrating tangible local benefits rather than relying on lobbying efforts in Washington. According to Nadella, concerns around electricity usage, infrastructure strain and local disruption can only be addressed through long-term engagement with communities."I don't think the public is getting it wrong," he said, adding that Microsoft's data centre expansion plans remain unchanged despite recent political developments.Nadella noted that the biggest constraints on data centre construction continue to be power availability, chip production capacity and memory supply rather than election outcomes.The Microsoft chief also addressed the massive Microsoft Outlook outage last week. The service disruption impacted the functioning of Teams, Copilot, SharePoint and other Microsoft 365 services. Nadella emphasised that the service disruption was not caused by any AI-generate code other AI deployments. Instead, he said that it was a ‘perfect story’ in which a software bug emerged during routine testing under specific web traffic conditions.He further stated that the internal tools at Microsoft actually helped the engineers to diagnose the issue and then resolve the problem.Apart from Huang, Nadella also talked about the recent voluntary buyout offer of Microsoft which was extended to almost 60,000 employees. As per the Microsoft CEO, the programme was aimed to offer more control to the workers over their career decisions instead of leaving them uncertain about the future when it comes to organisational changes. "There are some teams that are changing faster, some teams that are in a different place," Nadella said, referring to the varying pace of transformation across different parts of Microsoft.
Article Summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has expressed his admiration for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Huang stepped down as Nvidia CEO last week amid controversy surrounding revelations about his personal life. Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones subsequently indicated that the company had no plans to bring Huang back to the top role.

Article Title: Apple revamps Maps in India with street views, speed limits, and local-language labels
Article Text:
Apple rolls out all-new map across India

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Finding the right turn in India often means looking for a petrol pump or a flyover pillar rather than a street sign. Apple is bringing those familiar cues to Maps, rolling out a rebuilt India map with landmark-based directions, street-level imagery and labels in English and local languages.The update announced on Wednesday gives Apple a stronger offering in a market where finding the right turn can involve distinguishing a service lane from a flyover or locating an entrance on an unnamed road. Winning regular users, however, will depend on how reliably it handles those everyday journeys.Apple has expanded its conversational navigation instructions in India to refer to petrol pumps, pillars and other recognisable points along a route. Lane guidance is intended to help drivers position themselves before a turn or an elevated road. Users can also plan journeys with up to 15 stops.The company said the rebuilt map offers more accurate navigation and greater detail on roads, buildings, parks and shopping centres. It did not provide comparative accuracy figures or explain how frequently road changes would be incorporated.“We’ve also designed the map for India’s specific navigation needs, including enhanced Natural Language Guidance and customised dual-language labels,” said Max Muller, Apple’s vice-president of Apple Maps.Labels combine the device’s language with the local language of the area being viewed. Someone using an English-language iPhone would see Hindi alongside English in Delhi and Marathi alongside English in Mumbai. Apple said Maps now supports 11 languages used in India.Look Around, Apple’s interactive street-level imagery feature, is also arriving in India, alongside more than 300 three-dimensional landmarks. Augmented-reality walking directions allow users to scan nearby buildings with an iPhone to establish their position and see instructions overlaid on their surroundings.Public transport directions cover Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Delhi, Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and Pune, as well as Indian Railways. Travellers can find stations, save routes and receive alerts when they need to get off.Drivers can report accidents, hazards and speed checks through Siri, while arrival-time sharing updates friends or family if a journey is significantly delayed. Charging stops can be incorporated into routes for certain compatible electric vehicles, although the announcement did not identify supported models in India.Cycling directions, custom routes and previews of frequently taken commutes round out the update. Apple said commute learning happens on the device.The overhaul puts Apple up against Google Maps, the default navigation choice for many Indians, including iPhone users. Getting them to switch will require more than sharper imagery: Apple will have to match the everyday usefulness of Google’s business listings, traffic information and local search, while giving users a compelling reason to change a familiar habit.
Article Summary: Apple rolls out rebuilt India map with landmark-based directions, street-level imagery and labels in English and local languages. Lane guidance is intended to help drivers position themselves before a turn or an elevated road. Users can also plan journeys with up to 15 stops.
